questions.q: What is the condition for productive efficiency?
options: Output at the lowest point of the ATC curve
questions.why: Average cost is as low as it can be.

questions.q: What is the condition for allocative efficiency?
questions.why: The value of the last unit equals the cost of making it.

questions.q: Match each change to the kind of efficiency.
pairs: A firm moves to the lowest point of ATC
Price is brought down to equal MC
Research leads to a better product over ten years
questions.why: Productive and allocative are static, at a point in time. Dynamic is over time.

questions.q: Dynamic efficiency is influenced by research and development, investment and technological change.
questions.why: These improve resource use over time.

questions.q: Which structure is both productively and allocatively efficient in long-run equilibrium?
questions.why: P = MC at the lowest point of ATC. The others have P above MC.

questions.q: Explain why a firm in an oligopoly may be more dynamically efficient than one in perfect competition.

ideas.label: Oligopolists have abnormal profits to fund research
Firms in perfect competition make only normal profit, or rivalry and barriers reward innovation

questions.model: Oligopolists can earn abnormal profits to fund research. Rivalry gives them a reason to innovate, and barriers let them keep the gains, while perfectly competitive firms make only normal profit.
questions.why: Dynamic efficiency needs the money and the motive.

tests.answer: Abnormal profits fund research, while firms in perfect competition only make normal profit.
